interpretation: In this single serial pair, the corrected fresh device retained one queue node and metadata-only CloseHandle duration was substantially lower. Combined with observed missing initialization and restored reuse, this supports excess queue accumulation as a contributor to this device handle-close cost.
limitations: One uncorrected-then-corrected pair with different exposure times and incomplete retired-device teardown; order and background activity are not controlled.
Queue counts are debugger snapshots before the benchmark and after operator transfer, not exact per-call populations or exact queue growth rates.
Metadata-only handles differ from x86 XInput access and enumeration IOCTLs; the benchmark is x64, not the contributor's x86 game workload.
Open latency did not show the same improvement: corrected median and p95 were higher; do not claim a universal speedup for all operations.
Timing includes interop, scheduling and last-error retrieval. Sample caps ended both runs before the five-second limit.
GameInput service state and PID match in post-run inventories; complete service/activity continuity was not independently measured.
Hands-off controller activity was requested but not independently measured. Input fidelity, vibration and recovery remain untested.
These are live data corrections for one requestor in disposable device lifetimes, not a driver-file patch, installed fix or supported release.
Guest inbox is 0.2309.19041.5794, differing from contributor 0.2309.19041.6456. The contributor's FPS loss has not been reproduced or corrected here.
Ratio and reduction describe this pair's observed durations, not statistical confidence, game FPS improvement, hardware acceptance gates or general Windows-version coverage.
